intuition: The array was sorted before it was rotated. Around any middle position, at least one side is still sorted. Identify that side and check whether its value range includes the target. This tells us which half to keep without scanning every number.

At most one rotation drop appears inside the candidate interval. If nums[left] is no larger than nums[mid], the left half has no drop and is sorted. A target between those endpoint values belongs there; all other targets must be sought in the right half. When the left half is not sorted, the right half is.
Distinct values remove ambiguous equal-boundary cases and guarantee a substantial reduction on every iteration.

The target, if present, remains inside the candidate interval. A sorted half either contains the target in its numeric range or cannot contain it, so discarding the appropriate half preserves the invariant. The interval shrinks each iteration; exhaustion proves absence. Each iteration discards at least half the candidate positions.

steps: For [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], left=0, right=6, and mid=3 stores 7.
The left half [4,5,6,7] is sorted, but target 0 is outside its value interval.
The left half [0,1] is sorted and contains target 0, so right becomes 4.
Now mid=4 equals the target; return index 4.

concept.question: How does a broken sorted row still let us discard half the search?
intuition: A rotation breaks the global sorted order, so ordinary midpoint comparisons alone are insufficient. Scanning works, but wastes a useful fact: around a midpoint, at least one side is still sorted.

Find the side that is sorted. Its two endpoint values tell whether the target could lie inside. Keep that side only if its range contains the target; otherwise keep the other side. Distinct values make the sorted-side decision unambiguous.
concept.observation: Use the sorted side’s value range to decide which half can contain the target.
approach: Inspect the middle value and return its position if it matches.
Identify a sorted half using the endpoint values.
Keep the half whose range can contain the target, and repeat.
concept.correctness: Rotation divides a distinct sorted row into at most two ordered runs. At each midpoint, one side lies within a single run. If its ordered endpoint range excludes the target, the entire side is impossible; if it includes the target, distinct sorted order excludes the opposite side. Each safe half-discard preserves the target when present.

complexity.explanation: Every decision removes roughly half the remaining candidates. Work grows logarithmically with row length, and only a few positions and boundary values are remembered.

pitfalls: Use inclusive and exclusive range boundaries consistently.
Return an original position, not the target value.
